result.error_summary: Python can't find the pandas package, so app.py stops on its first import.
result.likely_cause: pandas isn't installed in the Python environment that ran app.py, or a different virtual environment is active.
alternative_causes: pip installed pandas for a different Python version than the one running the script.
fix_steps: Check which Python is running with `python --version`.
Activate the virtual environment you meant to use, if any.
Install pandas with that same Python.
Run `python app.py` again.
prevention_tips: Create one virtual environment per project and activate it before installing.
Install with `python -m pip` so packages go to the interpreter you actually run.
List dependencies in requirements.txt so a new machine can reinstall them in one command.
result.if_still_stuck: Run `python -m pip list` and confirm pandas appears in the list for this Python.

result.error_summary: UserList calls .map() on a value that is undefined, which crashes the component.
result.likely_cause: At UserList.jsx line 12 the code maps over a value that has no data yet. The screenshot doesn't show which variable it is, but it is usually a prop or state that hasn't loaded or wasn't passed in.
alternative_causes: The parent component isn't passing the prop under the name UserList expects.
fix_steps: Open UserList.jsx and go to line 12.
Find the array being mapped and check where its value comes from.
Give it a safe default so the first render doesn't crash.
Confirm the parent passes the prop, or that the data fetch sets the state.
result.code_fix:
// Replace yourArray with the value mapped on line 12 const items = (yourArray ?? []).map((item) =>
  • {item.name}
    • );
prevention_tips: Initialise array state with useState([]) rather than leaving it undefined.
Show a loading state until fetched data exists.
Add TypeScript types or PropTypes so a missing prop is caught early.
result.if_still_stuck: Add console.log on line 12 to print the value just before .map runs.

result.error_line: Error: Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {id, name, email}).
result.error_summary: ProfileCard is trying to render a whole object as text, which React can't display.
result.likely_cause: Inside ProfileCard, near line 9, a JSX expression outputs an object with the keys id, name and email instead of a string or number.
alternative_causes: A response object was passed to a component where plain text was expected.
fix_steps: Open ProfileCard.jsx and look near line 9 for a JSX expression that outputs the whole object.
Render a specific field of the object instead.
If you meant to show a list, map over it and return one element per item.
result.code_fix:
// Render a field of the object, not the object itself
{profile.name}
prevention_tips: Put strings and numbers in JSX, not whole objects.
Use JSON.stringify(value) only for temporary debugging output.
Type your props with TypeScript so this is caught before the app runs.
result.if_still_stuck: Search ProfileCard.jsx for curly braces that contain a single variable and check what each one holds.

result.error_summary: Node can't find the express package that server.js requires.
result.likely_cause: express isn't installed in the project's node_modules folder, or npm install was never run in /home/sairam/api.
alternative_causes: express is installed in a different folder from the one you start node in.
fix_steps: Go to the project folder that contains package.json.
Install the project's dependencies.
If express still isn't found, add it explicitly.
Run node server.js again.
prevention_tips: Run npm install after cloning a repository or pulling new changes.
Keep every dependency listed in package.json so npm install can restore it.
Don't commit node_modules; commit package-lock.json instead.
result.if_still_stuck: Run `npm ls express` to see whether npm can find the package from this folder.

result.error_line: ERROR 1064 (42000): You have an error in your SQL syntax
result.error_summary: MySQL can't run the query because the WHERE clause has no value after id =.
result.likely_cause: The condition `WHERE id = ;` is incomplete. A comparison needs a value on the right, so MySQL stops at the semicolon (near '' at line 1).
alternative_causes: If an application built this query, the variable that should hold the id was empty.
fix_steps: Add the value you want to compare id with.
Run the query again.
If your code builds the query, find out why the id was empty.
result.code_fix:
-- Replace 1 with the id you are looking for
SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE id = 1;
prevention_tips: Use parameterised queries in application code instead of joining strings.
Check that an id exists before running the query.
Build long queries in small pieces so the failing clause is easy to spot.
result.if_still_stuck: Read the text after `near` in the error: MySQL points at where parsing stopped.

result.tool_or_language: HTTP API request with curl in bash
result.error_summary: The API rejected the request because no valid API key was sent.
result.likely_cause: The curl command sends no credentials, and the www-authenticate header shows the API expects a Bearer token.
alternative_causes: A key was sent elsewhere but it is expired, revoked or for a different environment.
fix_steps: Get a valid API key or token from the API provider's dashboard.
Keep it in an environment variable instead of typing it into commands.
Send it in the Authorization header.
Run the request again.
prevention_tips: Keep keys in environment variables or a secrets manager, never in code or screenshots.
Rotate any key that was pasted into a chat, a commit or a screenshot.
Check the API docs for the exact header name before testing.
result.if_still_stuck: If you already send a key, regenerate it and check it belongs to the same environment as the URL.

result.error_summary: GitHub refused your push because the remote main branch has commits you don't have locally.
result.likely_cause: Someone (or you, from another machine or the GitHub website) pushed to main after your last pull.
fix_steps: Pull the remote changes into your local main.
Resolve any merge conflicts Git reports, then commit.
Push again.
prevention_tips: Pull before you start work and before you push.
Work on a feature branch and open a pull request instead of pushing to main.
result.if_still_stuck: Run `git status` to see whether a merge is half-finished, and `git log --oneline -5` to see what came in.

result.tool_or_language: Python in a VS Code PowerShell terminal
result.error_line: IndentationError: expected an indented block after 'for' statement on line 5
result.error_summary: The line after the for loop on line 5 isn't indented, so Python doesn't know it belongs to the loop.
result.likely_cause: The body of the for loop (the print on line 6) is at the same indentation level as the for statement itself.
alternative_causes: Tabs and spaces are mixed in main.py, so the indent isn't recognised.
fix_steps: Open main.py and go to line 6.
Indent the line by 4 spaces so it sits inside the for loop.
Use spaces only; in VS Code run 'Convert Indentation to Spaces' if unsure.
Save and run again.
result.code_fix: print("Total:", total)  # indented 4 spaces so it belongs to the loop
prevention_tips: Let your editor handle indentation and keep it to 4 spaces.
Turn on 'Render Whitespace' in VS Code to spot tabs mixed with spaces.
result.if_still_stuck: If the loop should do nothing for now, put `pass` on line 6 as a placeholder.
